offence_severity: Minimum 7 years to maximum 10 years for abducting and murdering (Section 302 IPC)
physical_harm: The victim was murdered by strangulation and cremated under a fictitious name
number_of_offences: Multiple offences charged; several counts upheld, including abducting, murdering, and conspiring
premeditation_planning: Yes, the plan was the brainchild of A1 and A2, and A3 organised the abduction and murder
key_evidence_accepted: The key evidence accepted by the Supreme Court includes the testimony of PW10 and PW11, the recovery of a nylon rope and chain, the cremation under a fictitious name, and the involvement of A3 in organizing the abduction and murder.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses (PW10 and PW11) as credible, noting that they had no motive to falsely implicate and their testimony brought home the truth. The accomplices were also considered credible witnesses despite their involvement in the crime.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused abducted the victim, illegally detained him, demanded a huge sum, and when the victim refused, he was strangled and murdered, with the body cremated under a fictitious name. The evidence included statements from PW10 and PW11, as well as other witnesses, and the recovery of a nylon rope and chain at the instance of A16.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court acquitted A10 and A12 based on circumstantial evidence, and that the evidence against other accused was not sufficient to prove their involvement in the murder. They also highlighted the lack of direct evidence relating to murder.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that after abduction, the abductor would be in a position to explain what happened to the victim, and if he failed to do so, an irresistible inference could be drawn that he committed the murder. The court also emphasized the requirement for corroboration of accomplice testimony under Section 133 of the Evidence Act.
precedent_relied_upon: K. Hashim v. State of Tamil Nadu (2005) 1 SCC 237; Haroom Haji Abdulla v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1968 SC 832; Sheshanna Bhumanna Yadav v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1970 SC 1330; Jagjit Singh v. State of Punjab (2018) 10 SCC 593; *Dalbir Kaur v. State of Punjab (1976) 4 SCC 158
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the evidence showing that the accused were involved in the abduction, illegal confinement, and murder of the victim, with the role of A3 being particularly significant in organizing the crime and ensuring the cremation under a fictitious name.
other_sentence_order: The bail bonds of the appellants who were released on bail under orders of this Court shall stand cancelled and they shall surrender within three weeks to serve their sentences.
